name: Multiple Wives
overview: Scripture presents the reality of multiple wives in the Old Testament, as seen in Lamech's example of taking two wives (Genesis 4:19) and the regulations given for such situations (Exodus 21:10; Deuteronomy 21:15). However, God's original design for marriage is one man united to one woman, becoming one flesh (Genesis 2:24). Furthermore, leaders are cautioned against multiplying wives to prevent their hearts from turning away (Deuteronomy 17:17), highlighting the ideal of faithfulness and singular devotion. Ultimately, finding a wife is portrayed as a good and God-favored blessing (Proverbs 18:22), emphasizing the value of the marital relationship within God's order.
